Header: Aspergillus flavus, Aspergillus nomius, Aspergillus parasiticus, Aspergillus tamarii Mirch ka Aflatoxin

Prevention: Aspergillus can feed and develop on dead leaves when vegetation is too lush.
Changes in harvesting practices, better screening of hand labour, and use of appropriate biologically stable barrier between soil and drying chilli.
Properly packed chillies should be stored in a damp-free, well-aerated store at (25– 28ºC).
Direct contact to soil should be avoided.
Containers must be clean, dry, and free of visible fungal growth, insects and any contaminated material.
Monitoring: ELISA testing at the farm gate to check toxicity levels and develop traceability protocols.
Moisture content and relative humidity should not be more than 14 and 60 percent, respectively in the stored area.
HPLC, high performance thin layer chromatograph, thin layer chromatograph and antibody-based ones are available for routine.
Use low-cost kits which are also being used in around 20 laboratories across the world to detect aflatoxin content.
Direct Control: Use of solar/ mechanical dryers or drying sheets.
Planting dates must be adjusted so that the crop matures at the end of the rainy season and post harvest conditions favour rapid and effective drying of crop
Restrictions: Keep pesticides out of reach of children
Always wear protective clothing, such as mask, rubber boots, gloves
Dispose of containers responsibly (Do not clean containers in canals)
Spray may be repeated at week interval if disease symtoms prevail.
Aflatoxin fungi may also be supressed with
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard for all chemicals)
